title: UAE's Nusseibeh comes in fourth in latest UNSG straw poll: What to know
gist: In the UN Security Council's seventh straw poll for the next secretary-general, Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan led (11 encourage, 4 discourage), followed by Argentina's Rafael Grossi, Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and the UAE's Lana Nusseibeh (7-6-2) in her first poll. Nusseibeh faces regional-rotation expectations favoring Latin America and criticism over alleged UAE support for Sudan's RSF; Guterres' term ends Dec. 31.

insights.claim: Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan led the UN Security Council's seventh secretary-general straw poll with 11 encourage and four discourage votes, per PassBlue.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Grynspan, who leads UNCTAD, is the frontrunner to head the UN from 2027.

insights.claim: Argentina's Rafael Grossi placed second with nine encourage and four discourage votes, and Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett third with eight encourage and six discourage.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Grossi's strong showing matters given his IAEA profile on Iran nuclear issues.

insights.claim: The UAE's Lana Nusseibeh received seven encourage, six discourage and two no-opinion votes in her first straw poll, placing fourth.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: A mid-pack debut gives the UAE a foothold but no clear path to the top UN post.

insights.claim: Uganda's Olara Otunnu, Ecuador's Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Ecuador's Ivonne A-Baki trailed with heavily discouraging tallies, A-Baki receiving 14 discourage votes.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: The field is narrowing to four realistic contenders.

insights.claim: An informal system of regional rotation has created expectations that the next UN secretary-general will come from Latin America or the Caribbean, alongside momentum to appoint the first woman.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Rotation norms structurally disadvantage the only MENA candidate.

insights.claim: More than 30 CELAC ambassadors held a press conference on Oct. 27 to reiterate that the next secretary-general should come from their region.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Organized regional bloc pressure lowers the odds of a non-Latin American pick.

insights.claim: Nusseibeh faces criticism from human rights groups and Sudanese advocates over the UAE's alleged support for Sudan's Rapid Support Forces, accusations a UN panel of experts found credible and the UAE denies.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Reputational exposure on Sudan could limit UAE soft-power gains and draw scrutiny of Gulf foreign policy.

insights.claim: Nusseibeh said stopping the conflict in Sudan will be the litmus test of the next UN secretary-general and would be her number one priority.
insights.speaker: Lana Nusseibeh
insights.so_what: Framing Sudan as a priority is an attempt to neutralize her main vulnerability.
insights.locator: She added that stopping the conflict

insights.claim: Nusseibeh is the only candidate from the Middle East and North Africa, nominated by the UAE on Oct. 21, and her candidacy has gained some momentum but faces significant hurdles.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: UAE's bid signals Gulf ambition for multilateral leadership roles.

insights.claim: A UN secretary-general candidate needs at least nine votes in the 15-member Security Council and must avoid a veto from any of the five permanent members: the US, China, the UK, France and Russia.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: P5 veto dynamics, especially US-China-Russia, will decide the final pick.

insights.claim: Turkey is considering nominating former Foreign Minister Feridun Sinirlioglu, current OSCE secretary-general, and the straw poll results could influence whether other countries enter the race.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Late entrants could scramble the race before Guterres' term ends Dec. 31.

insights.claim: Antonio Guterres' second five-year term ends Dec. 31, and the Security Council must recommend a candidate to the General Assembly, which formally appoints the secretary-general.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: A decision is due within weeks, setting UN leadership for global crisis diplomacy.
